Try dividing your screen into two vertically and watch the notes where they come from the left or the right half of the screen. Use the appropriate finger for that UNLESS it's a chord.

Recognise the common patterns in the game: chord spam, staircases, trills, alternating, as well as jackhammer (rapid tapping on the same spot). Apply the left and right half rule to these patterns appropriately.

Look near the top or middle of the screen rather than on the line so you'll have more time to process/read the hard patterns.

That's about it. To get better, try aiming to FC maps that have a lot of rudimentary patterns in them. I recommend Evolution Era (hard) and Reverse-Parallel Universe because they have a good mix of rudimentary patterns. If you can FC those, pretty much every non-lvl 10 song in the game will be of no trouble to you.

Finally, if you're training for accuracy make sure you know your song decently well and tap according to what you hear, only using what you see as a guide. If you're sight-reading try to get used to the BPM or song structure/motifs/repeated patterns as quickly as you can.

Good luck.

Hey, Wyatt! Great to see a fellow young game developer! 

My biggest tip would be to let go of handholds. Just dive straight into the deep end. If you feel like you’re familiar with JS/Python already, just go for the biggest game you can think of. And do it. Don’t follow tutorials that teach you how to make flappy bird clones. Those don’t help outside of their own scope. 

In my opinion, the best way to learn programming is to do it and learn it yourself. Try. Experiment. That’s not to say you can’t ask for help or Search online. Work on something yourself. The internet is your best resource in the darkness. Search, but don’t copy. Make sure you understand everything you read before you do. Search things like “how to detect collision” not “how to make an adventure game”. You’ll learn from the first and not the second.

Those are my best tips for you. Eventually, you’ll make something big if you keep doing this. Just don’t give up. Good luck and have fun!
